Subject: Recap + data ask: unit econ, token volumes, CAC payback

Hi Elise — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the pieces we said we'd capture so we can put together a short economics proposal.

Call recap (2-min):
- HealthSync wants to pilot two inference-driven features: (1) triage summarization for inbound messages, (2) automated patient outreach templates.
- Pilot target: 3 months, ~10k MAU for triage, ~25k monthly templates processed.
- Key vendor asks: target $/1M tokens goal, estimated per-feature gross margin target, and CAC payback expectation for the pilot-to-scale path.

Data ask (can you share by end of week?):
1) Current monthly message volume and average tokens per message (historical or estimate).
2) Expected growth during pilot and at 12-month scale.
3) Targeted commercial metrics: target $/1M tokens you hope to hit, and acceptable CAC payback window (months).
4) Any procurement constraints (PO terms, security questionnaire cadence) — flagged procurement@healthsync.com on this thread.

What we'll deliver: a short 2-slide unit-econ summary and two pricing options (pilot pricing + scale pricing) that map to both feature-level $/feature and $/1M tokens equivalency. I'll attach an initial cost workbook for our internal calc; feel free to drop numbers in.

Attachment: initial-cost-model.xlsx (workbook with token assumptions & pilot scale scenarios)

Next step: if you can share the numbers above, Ben and I will put together a proposed pricing table and a CAC-payback sensitivity table (best / base / conservative). I propose a 30-min follow-up next Tue to walk through — is 10am PT good?

Thanks,
Mina

Quick numbers:
- Current monthly messages (in-scope for triage): ~420k messages/month.
- Average tokens per message (after extraction): ~220 tokens (we ran a sample).
- Template sends (expected for outreach): ~18k/month on pilot, expecting 80k/mo at scale.
- Growth: pilot to scale ~4x within 9–12 months.
- Budget band for pilot tooling (licensing + infra): $12k–$25k/month — flexible if unit price drives clear ROI.
- CAC payback target: ~6–9 months for feature-driven acquiring improvements (our product team prefers <=9 months; execs push for 6 if possible).

Procurement note: procurement@healthsync.com will request SOC2 evidence and a short security addendum. We can coordinate timelines early.

For the pricing proposal, we want to see:
- A per-feature $/month plan vs a pure $/1M tokens equivalent so our finance folks can map to existing chargeback models.
- An explicit example showing how triage at 420k msgs/month maps to tokens and expected monthly charge at each pricing tier (pilot/scale).

10am PT Tue works for me to review the proposal. Looking forward to the pilot options.

—Elise

Internal draft notes before we send proposal to HealthSync:

Summary of external inputs: 420k msgs/mo * 220 tokens/msg = ~92.4M tokens/mo (triage only). Templates add ~ (18k * avg 450 tokens) ~= 8.1M tokens/mo. Total pilot token load ~100.5M tokens/mo. Scale target (~4x) => ~402M tokens/mo.

Redwood unit-cost assumptions (rough, to validate with infra):
- Hosted baseline cost to Redwood (approx): $0.90 per 1M tokens (quantized, batched flows) — conservative nod to latency SLOs.
- Variable infra+ops overhead: $0.15 per 1M tokens.
- Total unit cost to Redwood: ~$1.05 per 1M tokens (pilot).

Pricing constructs to propose (we want two clear routes):
Option A — Pilot-focused (commit 3 months):
- Discounted blended price: $6.5 / 1M tokens (intro) — justification: rapid onboarding, lower SLA commitment, shared pilot support.
- Equivalent per-feature mapping example: triage (420k msgs) => ~100.5M tokens => ~$653 / month at $6.5 per 1M tokens (pilot). (Wait: math check — this looks off, recalc in final doc.)

Option B — Scale (12-month commit, reserved capacity):
- Reserved pricing: $2.8 / 1M tokens (volume-driven, SLA-backed), includes caching recommendations and a 3% quality holdback.
- Per-feature mapping: triage at scale (~402M tokens) => ~$1,126 / month at $2.8 per 1M tokens (again to be recalculated in proposal).

CAC payback framing:
- If HealthSync's unit economics for patient acquisition improves by even a small percent, a $12k/month budget can be payback-positive based on our estimated LTV uplift. Need them to confirm expected revenue per acquired patient.

Action items for Mina before Tue:
- Recalculate per-feature monthly charges with correct arithmetic and include a worked example for 420k messages (pilot) and 4x scale.
- Prepare three pricing buckets (pilot, reserved, enterprise) with explicit $/1M mapping and a simple CAC-payback table (months-to-payback at 5%, 10%, 20% uplift).
- Include a line for sample contract terms (PO net-30 default, SOC2 evidence doc link).

I'll proof the slide + numbers after you draft.

—Ben

Subject: Proposal & next steps — HealthSync pilot economics (slides + examples)

Hi Elise — attaching a short proposal and corrected worked examples based on Ben's notes. Key points listed below so finance/procurement can map quickly.

Worked examples (corrected arithmetic):
- Pilot load (triage + templates): ~100.5M tokens/month.
- Option A (pilot intro): $6.50 per 1M tokens => monthly charge = 100.5 * $6.50 = $653.25 (note: this is per 1M units; we've used a shorthand where '100.5' means 100.5 units of 1M tokens).
- Option B (reserved at scale): $2.80 per 1M tokens => at scale ~402M tokens => 402 * $2.80 = $1,125.60/month.

Pricing notes and mapping to $/feature:
- Triage (per-message cost): with pilot pricing, triage per-message incremental = (100.5M tokens / 420k msgs) => ~239 tokens/msg * $6.50/1M => ~$0.00155 per message. Multiply by expected adds to get per-feature monthly cost.
- Templates (outreach): lower per-item token count when templated and cached; we show both cold and cached variants in the attached slides.

CAC payback sensitivity (summary):
- Using HealthSync's stated budget band ($12k–$25k/mo) and an assumed revenue per acquired patient of $90:
  - 5% uplift => months to payback: 10–20 months (depends on pricing tier).
  - 10% uplift => months to payback: 5–10 months.
  - To meet the 6–9 month target, we recommend Option B at scale economics OR adding outcome-based kicker tied to acquisition lift.

Attachments: redwood-proposal-3-options.pdf (2-slide summary + worked examples).

Next steps:
1) Elise/procurement: confirm whether PO/net-30 is fine and share any required KBA/Security contact for SOC2 exchange.
2) HealthSync: provide expected revenue per acquired patient (or attach typical LTV) and confirm acceptance of the three pricing buckets as a starting point.
3) Agree follow-up: Tue 10am PT to review the deck (confirmed).

Thanks — sending the slide deck now. If you want a quick pre-call run at 9:30am PT Tue, Ben and I can be available.

Best,
Mina
